convoLines.text: "I hate to ask this, but whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Can you do anything?"
"The fever's not breaking and I'm barely keeping food down. I need help — real help, not just water."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I dreamed Luigi was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"All right —" Greta starts to stand, then sinks back down. "Maybe not today. The fire's got me."
"I do push-ups at dawn. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Felix digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1503 kcal to the pantry.)
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"I, uh — Still on their secret."
They relax, a fraction. This is going well.
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Luigi owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hey — I found some Stinging Nettle today. You were right, it was right where you said, anyway."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. Felix doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that plant lesson."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Luigi is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Sleep's gone strange. I check everyone's shoes for wear at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Birds went quiet an hour before it spoke the first time. They knew. Animals always know first."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet. Doesn't matter now."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Alejandro doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Ha." Not amused. "I wasn't a rail conductor. I was a piano tuner. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others. There. You happy?"
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
"I dreamed Greta was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I count portions out loud before eating. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"The fire feels smaller without Greta. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Watch this — Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Felix. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Greta owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
"I check everyone's shoes for wear for Greta, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You're one of the good ones. Don't make me regret saying that out loud." "Don't make me say it twice."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.

"It's my aunt, Rebecca. Went in the Taking. She laughed like a screen door in a windstorm. Boring. Right. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Lena — The Pit, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
«C'est quoi, cet endroit ? Où sommes-nous ?» "Shit." — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
"Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane… That's Old Croaker telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"This one — Feral Paddy Rice. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
«D'accord.» They nod back, slowly.
«T'es un amour, merci.» (you catch 'amour' — darling) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Merci. Vraiment, merci.» (you catch 'Merci' — thanks) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «C'est toi... le chef ?» (you catch 'chef' — boss)
Valentin laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — D'accord.." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
